title: Principality of Koknese
capsule: The Principality of Koknese (Kokenhusen) was a small vassal state of the Principality of Polotsk situated on the lower Daugava River in present-day Latvia, ruled in the late 12th and early 13th centuries by Prince Vetseke. As the Livonian crusade intensified under Bishop Albert of Riga, Vetseke ceded half his territory to the bishop in 1205 seeking protection, then rebelled, burned Koknese Castle to deny it to the crusaders, and fled to Novgorod c. 1207–1209. The Livonian Brothers of the Sword occupied the site, and by 1238 the territory passed formally to the Bishopric of Riga.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The principality is attested in Henry of Latvia's chronicle and Livonian crusade documents; its territory is approximately identifiable but precise boundaries are not cartographically fixed.
